# QS-CFW-5042-83 Quality specification - valve body CFW-5042-83 (F316)

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3  
Part: CFW-5042-83

Scope
This quality specification applies to the forged valve body CFW-5042-83 produced in Plant P3 from material grade F316. It establishes the mandatory acceptance requirements, the required inspection methods, and the process for managing nonconforming items. The purpose is to ensure forged parts meet functional and metallurgical criteria prior to machining and assembly, and that inspection records provide traceability for production and corrective action.

Requirements table
The following table lists the mandatory acceptance criteria for the valve body CFW-5042-83. These attributes are verified at final forge inspection and any subsequent operations that could affect the attribute.

| Attribute | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hardness range | 33-38 HRC | Hardness measured in the parent forged material, away from finish-machined surfaces. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.06 mm | Applies to the as-forged bore prior to final machining; control dimension for downstream fixtures. |
| Maximum forging weight | 77.3 kg | Net forging weight after flash removal and trimming, prior to heat treat and finish machining. |

Inspection method
General approach
Inspection shall be performed by qualified inspection personnel using calibrated instruments appropriate to each attribute. The inspection location is the final forge inspection area prior to heat treatment and machining. Records of inspections shall be retained with the heat lot and forging serial reference.

Hardness measurement
- Hardness testing shall be performed on representative forged surfaces in the parent metal, avoiding areas affected by trimming, heavy deformation, or tooling marks. Test locations shall be documented on the part record. Use a standardized hardness method suitable for HRC scale. Report measured values and note any readings outside the stated hardness range of 33-38 HRC. When borderline readings are encountered, additional tests on adjacent locations are documented until a clear condition is established. All hardness readings, test instrument identification, and calibration references are recorded on the inspection sheet.

Bore diameter verification
- The bore diameter tolerance of ±0.06 mm applies to the as-forged bore prior to machining. Bore inspection is performed with instruments capable of resolving to the tolerance band and set up to verify roundness and concentricity where applicable. Record the measured bore size, measurement method, and instrument identification. If the as-forged bore falls outside ±0.06 mm, the part is treated as nonconforming and handled per the Nonconformance handling section.

Weight confirmation
- Maximum forging weight is recorded after trimming and flash removal and prior to any subsequent heat treatment or machining. The maximum forging weight limit is 77.3 kg. The forging weight is documented on the production record; parts exceeding the maximum forging weight are identified and segregated for review.

Record keeping
- For each inspected lot, records shall include part identification CFW-5042-83, plant P3, heat lot, inspector identity, inspection date and time expressed in local plant format, instrument identifiers, calibration status, measured values for hardness, bore diameter, and forging weight, and any deviation notes. These records are retained in the document control system in association with the forging lot and made available for quality audits and engineering review.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation
Nonconforming items are controlled to prevent unintended use. Any part that fails to meet one or more requirements in the Requirements table is to be clearly identified and segregated from conforming stock. The nonconforming condition, referring to the specific attribute and measured value, is recorded on the nonconformance tag and the lot record.

Disposition
Disposition options include documented repair, rework, or rejection. Repair and rework actions that could affect metallurgical properties or critical dimensions require engineering review and formal disposition authorization before implementation. For hardness and weight issues, the impact on material properties and downstream processing must be evaluated by engineering. For bore diameter deviations, assess whether corrective machining or rework is practicable without compromising part integrity or functional dimensions after machining.

Examples
- Example: If a part measures below the hardness range of 33-38 HRC, evaluate whether heat treatment variation or material batch condition caused the deviation. Document the investigation and disposition. Record all hardness readings and any corrective actions taken.
- Example: If a part exceeds the maximum forging weight of 77.3 kg after trimming, segregate the part and initiate an investigation into forging parameters and trimming process. Record the measured weight and investigation outcome.

Corrective action and root cause
For repeated or systemic nonconformance, initiate a root cause analysis and corrective action plan. The corrective action record shall reference the affected heat lots and production runs, the measured deviations (as recorded for hardness, bore diameter, or weight), actions taken to prevent recurrence, and verification of effectiveness. All corrective action documentation is linked to the forging lot record.

Disposition authority and records
Only authorized personnel may sign off dispositions. The disposition record shall include the nonconformance description, measured value(s), disposition selected, signatures of reviewer and approver, and references to any engineering approval. Disposition records are maintained with the part history for traceability.

Revision control
This document is controlled under the plant document control system. Changes to inspection methods or acceptance requirements must be approved through the established revision procedure and applied to new production lots only after release.

End of specification.
